utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The first part of this intervention that the Defence has to do in open session and the second matter we will do in closed session, when we return to closed session, because it may concern some elements linked to that. The issue that the Defence would like to raise is the respect of the procedure on a particular point which is the administration, the production of evidence. Although, the Rule doesn't say anything about the time in which an exhibit has to be tendered to the file. We can start from the principle or we can assume that it should be tendered in relation to and at the same time, concurrently with the testimony of a witness or witnesses that it concerns. There would be no sense, Mr. President otherwise to hear witnesses and then not to tender exhibits or not to be able to discuss the exhibits, except for several weeks later or several months later, depending on the proceedings. So the Rule is Witness and exhibits. Now, having said that, we have had a problem which is a problem of size, a series of exhibits, because all of the exhibits have the same -- seem to have the same -- afflicted in the same way, which is grattage, although your Chamber has not yet decided on the admissibility of these exhibits. So what we have asked is that the Prosecution informs us of all the steps that they have taken or that they were able to take in relation to a matter, that is, what happened. So what happened in relation to these manipulations. Now, the Prosecution has given us reports, which is very short, three or four chapters only, where we are not enlighten in any way on this matter. The only thing that we are being told, do not worry about it, everything is going for the best -- in the best of the worlds and it seems that the people will be able to confirm that the date is exactly the one we say it is. Now, Mr. President, what we wanted is not to have this, but to have and throw some light for your Chamber and for us on the question on how these manipulations were done, how they could have been done. Since nothing was done whether this was voluntarily or not, but this is the fact, Mr. President. We, therefore, believe that the Defence cannot be forever suspended in midair knowing whether these exhibits are being tendered or not and we therefore believe that it is necessary for your Chamber to make a decision and your Chamber has to take this decision today. Are we to accept this in this trial in relation to an element which is important on the -- regarding the theory of the shelling of the Prosecution. When we look at the dozens of pieces and what is proven is that there have been manipulations to date. If this is a question asked by the Defence, the Defence can say that on our side we know the answer well and that it is not admissible that the exhibits that have all been manipulated be tendered, be accepted, admitted by this Chamber. Now, what we are asking your Chamber is that to have a decision very shortly in which the Chamber would reject all the exhibits, and I mean all of them, their entirety, I am talking about exhibits in relation to Markale incident, all of the exhibits that were tendered by the Prosecution, produced by the Prosecution which are all product of a manipulation. This, Mr. President, is the submission of the Defence and if we can have that decision as soon as possible. We are asking this because there could be other witnesses appearing in relation to Markale. And as long as we don't know which side it is going, the Defence is in a situation of technical inferiority, since we do not know your decision on a very important part which is the exhibits for the Markale incident. Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will discuss the matter with my colleagues and the Chamber will let you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there are a number of matters that I wish to raise. I do not seek to raise them now. I would seek to raise them at the conclusion of the evidence of Witness W. They have to do with the trial time table and the like and I am happy to respond to what my learned colleague has said at that time as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you had another issue to be raised in closed session?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like now to turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, the Prosecution is experiencing extreme difficulty in keeping to the time table which requires us to finish our case by the 5th of July. I had hoped to raise this issue yesterday, as I indeed anticipated I would last week. It became clear yesterday that a greater priority was to continue with evidence in closed session. I, therefore, had in mind to raise that issue, principally, together with some others today, in between our closed session evidence and the recalling of Mr. Mole. I no longer have confidence that there will be an opportunity today. Mr. President, the Prosecution would be grateful if time could be found before tomorrow afternoon to hear submissions on this issue, this principal issue. The Prosecution could then take advantage of next week, when we are not sitting, to reorganise its case. It seems to me that, having regard to the time table for tomorrow, that is, the calling of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. General Van Baal and the special requirements which have been put in place for his evidence, that we will not have an opportunity between 9.00 and 1.45 p.m. tomorrow. Therefore, the only remaining possibilities are either this afternoon in a different courtroom or tomorrow morning before 9.00 or tomorrow afternoon after 1.45. And I say that, of course, mindful of the lack of notice to you, Mr. President and Your Honours, and to the Registry. I would not make this application were it not for the fact that it is a matter of, in my view, extreme urgency. I intimated yesterday that I had been approached by the head of the Victims and Witnesses Unit and indeed met with her to hear from her their concerns as to the pressure which they are under in this case and of course which one can readily understand, given the changes on a daily basis to the witness schedule. Mr. President, I don't seek to venture into making submissions at this stage. I simply seek an opportunity to do so. It seems to me that if we did it in written submissions, it would take too long, having regard to the need to give time to the Defence to consider our written submissions. Rather, practically, it is best done, if it meets with your approval, if we have an opportunity to do so early. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. First of all, as a matter of fact, we are, in relation to the proceedings, in the middle of our life's journey, so to speak, and in fact, the way I understand the Prosecution's argument, Prosecution has reason to be more and more concerned, and I do agree that they should be concerned. However, Mr. President, the fact is that the Prosecution is creating these difficulties. We have seen this today, and it is not up to the Defence to bear the consequences. One example --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the issue is whether we could find a place and a time by tomorrow. Who is to blame for the situation, I think the Chamber is perfectly aware that there is never a black and white situation. So we don't have to discuss this at that moment, at this moment, but can we find a place and a time to discuss the issues raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will answer your question. There are two orders on your -- two responses -- motions regarding the Prosecution motions. I have not been able to look at them until last night 2.00 a.m. Now, I am being asked to work full steam ahead. Now, last week I had to wear sunglasses, not because of style, but my eyes were not allowing me any more to see the transcript. Now, if this is what the situation is, that is very well, but we do have to breathe occasionally. Yes, occasionally in fact. And we cannot accept this situation. And I am very sorry, but the only means that we have is to stop the counterattack and to gain time and to continue, but we cannot go on working until 2.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will consider your request, Mr. Ierace, and we will let you know by today. If we would hear your submissions on the time schedule, we would have to find a place and a time. Is there anything else to be raised in open session?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will then turn into closed session again, but not yet ask the witness to come in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, as you -- we are not yet in open session? We are now. Mr. Ierace, there will not be enough time to discuss the matter today. If, however you would have in mind, for example, you can say I am going to ask you tomorrow for one week extra or we can do it in two days less, could you indicate if that would be the case and not to start a debate at this moment, but at least to give everyone already an opportunity to think about it. What is it that you were going to ask us tomorrow, within 30 seconds, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, five extra weeks. And I should also indicate that we have learned that Mr. Van Baal will not be available until 11.00 a.m. at the earliest. It appears there was some misunderstanding as to whether tomorrow's session would be morning or afternoon. I apologise to the Trial Chamber for that. Mr. Mole has been waiting around since Monday, but perhaps in the circumstances, the period of time, the one and a half hours before Mr. Van Baal's evidence could be ultimately more profitably used by resolving this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber cannot promise you that a decision on five weeks could be taken in three hours. Tomorrow, I think, Madam Registrar, we are not going to change the schedule any more. We start at 8.30 tomorrow morning. We gain that half an hour. The breaks will, however, be at different times from usual because that is also in respect of the interpreters and those who are assisting us. But we will finish at the same time as usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President given that Mr. Van Baal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Piletta-Zanin was now first. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Thank you very much. Simply to say that it would be good if you -- if we can be let know who should we expect tomorrow if Defence could be told who we can expect so we can prepare ourself. You know the Defence sometimes is not quite prepared. If we have one or the other witness, that will change our preparation

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...we will start at Mr. Mole the continuation of the examination-in-chief at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I could do that but we will not finish Mr. Mole tomorrow. There seems little point in having another hour or so his evidence tomorrow and then he will have to come back anyway in some weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there no way of getting Mr. Van Baal earlier than 11.00? I mean he lives nearby, I take it. Would there be no way of starting earlier so that we can finish the testimony. I think he is scheduled for two hours, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I would not be surprised if even if he started at 9.00. He did not finish tomorrow, I have to say that, based on what has happened time and again over the last few weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is another thing. I will call upon the parties. Of course we had less problems than we had with the previous witness for reasons everyone will understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will try, Mr. President. I will try to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there would be a possibility to get Mr. Van Baal at 9.00. We will start anyhow at 8.30 and we will see whether Mr. Van Baal can come at 9.00. We will now adjourn until tomorrow morning, 8.30 --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do apologise. Assuming that General Van Baal is not available until 11.00 or 10.00 or whenever, is it your preference that we call Richard Mole for that intervening period or that we do not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is just the examination-in-chief, and if he is there -- and of course I have no idea on the line of questioning. If you would have the stop in the middle of a line of questions, then, of course, we could better wait until he is back. Let's try to use our time as efficiently as possible. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. In order to be as courteous as possible, including the Prosecution and Mr. Van Baal the Defence would like to complain about the fact, once again, that we have only been given the translations in relation to Mr. Van Baal just a moment ago. I am talking about translation into Serbo-Croatian and it is absolutely impossible, respecting the normal proceedings, if what General Galic has just reminded me of, is that he does not have the possibility of seeing what this person could have said or what he is going to say, this is not normal fair play because if every time I have to stand up and repeat it, and now in a way of repeating myself, every time it is the very same story. I think you have understood me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the statement -- let's not discuss the matter at this very moment. We will think it over and we have to leave this courtroom because another case will be heard. But I took notice of your complaint that the translation has been provided only today or yesterday -- today --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- was not informed one week ago that you were waiting for this translation. We will adjourn until tomorrow morning, 8.30, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1.50 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 7th day of June, 2002, at 8.30 a.m. 23 24 25
